findings.title: Org 'ignores attribution values sent in the request body' proves copy-from-user wins, not that strong params rejects the body value
findings.description: The test sends body organization.utm_source='attacker' with current_user.utm_source='SomeRawValue' and asserts the persisted value is 'SomeRawValue'. This IS falsifiable against the feature (delete the four @organization.utm_source = current_user.* lines and the result becomes nil since organization_params does not permit utm_source, so 'attacker' is dropped by strong params and nothing sets it — nil != 'SomeRawValue' fails). So it is not a ghost test. However, the explicit override on organizations_controller.rb:32 always wins, so this assertion would still pass 'SomeRawValue' even in the hypothetical where organization_params DID permit utm_source (a strong-params leak). The test therefore does not independently prove the body value is rejected by organization_params — it proves the current_user copy produces the final value. No actual gap exists because utm_source is genuinely not in the permit list (organizations_controller.rb:119), so this is an observation, not a defect. Optional strengthening: also assert organization_params does not permit utm_source, or use a body value distinguishable from both the user value and nil.
findings.recommendation: Optional: add a separate assertion that the request body's utm_source is not permitted (e.g., that a fresh org built from organization_params alone has nil utm_source), so the 'ignores body' claim is proven at the strong-params layer independent of the copy override. Not required for correctness.

notes: GHOST-TEST / falsifiability walk of every it block. registrations_controller_spec.rb: (1) magic_create new-user 'stores four raw' (L30) — POSITIVE, FALSIFIABLE: params are flat (email/utm_* at top level), matching sign_up_params flat permit (controller L310); login_intent:'hire' takes the else merge branch (controller L102-115, verified in git diff 62dd55867..fc3f047f9) which sets the four utm keys; organization nil (no organization_slug) so add_connect_user is skipped (no M2 crash) and active_for_authentication? is true (organization.nil?), reaching build_resource+save; deleting the merge or the sign_up_params utm permit yields nil and fails the eq assertions. utm_data assertion uses STRING keys ({'utm_medium'=>'email','utm_term'=>'hiring'}) and reads via fresh User.find_by (DB round-trip of jsonb → string keys), so the expectation matches; a symbol-keyed expectation would have been wrong — they got it right. (2/6) magic_create + create 'leaves nil when none sent' (L50, L147) — NEGATIVE CONTROLS: pass with the feature deleted, but they are legitimate paired guards against value fabrication (a `|| {}` / default-{} regression on utm_data), which the spec comment explicitly targets ('utm_data stays nil, never {}'); schema confirms user.utm_data jsonb has NO default (nil), so absent input truly stays nil and the test can fail if a fabrication bug is introduced — not a harmful ghost. (3) confirmed-user 'does not modify' (L68) and (4) unconfirmed-user 'resends, does not modify' (L97) — NEGATIVE: those branches (controller L119 confirmed, L146 unconfirmed) never touch utm; both return :ok; guards against a bug writing utm on those branches; legitimate. (5) create 'persists via sign_up_params' (L127) — POSITIVE, FALSIFIABLE: sign_up_params.merge → build_resource; delete the utm permit → nil → fails; create has no recaptcha; user has no org so active_for_authentication? true, jobs enqueued (test adapter). DEVISE MAPPING (rule 30): spec has BOTH include Devise::Test::ControllerHelpers (L15) AND before { @request.env['devise.mapping'] = Devise.mappings[:api_v1_user] } (L24-26); mapping name :api_v1_user is correct (routes.rb:123 devise_for :users under namespace api/v1 + devise_scope :api_v1_user); the before hook sets the mapping on @request BEFORE dispatch, so the DeviseController prepend_before_action assert_is_devise_resource! finds it — no AbstractController::ActionNotFound. QUEUE ADAPTER (rule 31): around block saves original adapter, sets :test, restores (L17-22) — matches bulk_ai_job_application_summaries precedent; prevents PosthogIdentifyJob/PosthogTrackJob/enqueue_complete_user_setup from firing inline. RECAPTCHA: Recaptcha::Verifier#verify returns VerificationResult.new(true) immediately when Rails.env.test? (verifier.rb:16), so magic_create passes without a token — the :ok assertions hold and tests run green. organizations_controller_spec.rb: 'copies all four from current_user' (L40) — POSITIVE, FALSIFIABLE: delete the four copy lines (controller L32-35, confirmed as the feature delta) → columns nil → eq fails. 'nil user creates org with nil' (L77) — NEGATIVE control against fabrication; legitimate. AUTH STUBBING correct & NOT a DeviseController: BaseController before_actions are exactly authenticate_api_v1_user! + set_sentry_context (both stubbed L18-21), and create calls authorize @organization (stubbed true); ApplicationController includes Pundit but has NO after_action :verify_authorized (only rescue_from Pundit::NotAuthorizedError), so the authorize stub does NOT trigger an AuthorizationNotPerformedError — org spec runs. STUB TYPE-MATCH (rule 7): no external-API stubs in either spec; current_user stub returns a real persisted User record so .utm_source/.utm_data/.id are real. Org save succeeds: Organization validates name presence + nil-safe validate_wwr_percent_off (returns early when settings blank), org built with name+owner_id saves → :ok. jsonb round-trip: organization.utm_data compared as {'utm_medium'=>'email'} string keys via fresh Organization.find_by — correct. CONCLUSION: no ghost tests, no dispatch-failing specs, no stub mismatches; the three positive tests are properly falsifiable and the negative controls are legitimate absence/fabrication guards. One LOW observation on the strength of the org body-tamper test (F1), no real defect.
